title: an attributed namespace re-export of an asset compiles and the asset is still loaded at compile time
notes: The acceptance control for a-bare-star-re-export-of-an-asset-is-rejected. docs/ASSET_LOADERS.md lists 'attributed named/namespace re-exports' among the forms the compiler integrates, in the same sentence whose other half names 'bare star re-exports' as unsupported, so the two cases are the two halves of one documented boundary. Without this control an implementation that refused every `export ... from` on an asset would satisfy the refusal case exactly, and the corpus could not tell a correct implementation from one that had simply given up on asset re-exports — which is a live risk rather than a theoretical one, because the Go bridge's asset discovery and lowering were import-only until this session. Line 1 imports the same asset the line below re-exports, deliberately: it makes the re-export observable through OUTPUT rather than only through the absence of a diagnostic, and it pins that requesting one asset twice with identical attributes is one admitted asset rather than a conflicting-shape refusal. The printed line is the file's own value, so a loader that returned a path, a stub, or a runtime read would fail here; and per docs/ASSET_LOADERS.md (Locked) 'Loading happens during compilation. It does not add `FileSystem` or another runtime platform requirement to the importing program', so the emitted program must run with no `config.json` beside it — which is exactly what a-non-literal-dynamic-asset-import-is-rejected records the Go fork failing to do.
